name: setTCPNoDelay
title: Modify the TCP_NODELAY ('de-Nagle') flag for socket objects

origin.description: Turn Nagling off or on for a TCP socket.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Logical indicating whether to set (TRUE) or unset (FALSE) the flag.

origin.details: value = TRUE disables Nagle's algorithm. value = FALSE enables it. A nonzero number sets the flag, and as.integer truncation decides a fractional number. The call returns SUCCESS when setsockopt succeeds and errno is 0. After a failed call, a later success still changes the flag and returns the previous strerror text, because setsockopt does not clear errno. An object that is not a socket or a sockconn fails before that call. NA fails in the foreign call. A character value warns and then fails the same way.
origin.value: The status text, returned invisibly on success. A failed setsockopt stops with strerror.
origin.example:
socket <- make.socket("127.0.0.1", port)
print(socket)
print(setTCPNoDelay(socket, TRUE))

translation.description: Turn Nagling off or on for a TCP socket.

arguments.name: sock
arguments.text: A socket.socket, or a Socket whose socket field is the descriptor.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: True sets TCP_NODELAY. False, 0, or a truncated 0 clears it. None is logical NA.

translation.details: The call is setsockopt with IPPROTO_TCP and TCP_NODELAY. A nonzero value stores 1 and a zero stores 0. The first element of a list or tuple is the value, and any NA rejects the call. The returned text is SUCCESS when errno is 0. A successful call leaves errno unchanged, so after a failure the next success returns that strerror text and still updates the flag. Anything other than a socket.socket or a Socket raises before the call.
translation.value: The status text. A failed setsockopt raises RuntimeError with strerror.
translation.example:
from set_tcp_no_delay import setTCPNoDelay
print(setTCPNoDelay(client, True))
